main_body: Wooden column: a rounded cap disk (rows 8-14), a long shaft with two gold bands (rows 15-40), and a flared base (rows 41-47).
top_band: Light-tan rounded cap top at x=8, rows 9-12 (L=126-153, 4 rows), wider than the shaft with rounded corners. A darker lip follows at rows 13-14, then an outline at rows 15-16.
evidence: The cap is wider than the shaft and has rounded corners. Its lighter top rows 9-12 (about 4 rows) sit above a darker lip (rows 13-14) and a dark under-line (rows 15-16), which acts as the eave shadow. The shaft below is a shaded cylinder with a bright gold band at rows 20 and 35. The cap is only just lighter than the shaft, and at x=5 the two tones are nearly equal, so this is marginal. It still meets the column-cap rule of at least 4 rows, wider than the shaft, and lighter at the centre, so I judge it three-quarter.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours, against 38-40 in the references. Its median is 10 colours per tile, against 17 and 20 in the references. The outline is a dark brown, but 74% of its dark edge pixels measure near-neutral, so I call it mixed. The wood ramp has about 5 steps, and the shaft has some vertical-stripe shading and two gold bands, with no flat fills. Next to the stall and the roofed well it still reads thinner and less textured, with no per-material grain and a narrow palette. Being strict on the colour and density numbers, it fails.
